probeMissions: BASE, common to both missions: `node dist/cli.js init --yes --example` on runward 0.36.0 in an empty directory (that tree is green under `check --strict`). Then, per probe row: one house rule `runward/rules/<id>.md` whose frontmatter is `impact: MEDIUM` and `signature: <the shape>` and which declares NO phase (so no other pass looks at it — corpus divergence reports an unwritten rule only when it declares a gated phase at CRITICAL/HIGH, and the baseline confirms it: every conformance entry on the battery mission comes from a probe row, none from the corpus); one fixture `code/probe/<id>.txt` holding the content the compiled regex would run against; one row `| <id> | applied | file:code/probe/<id>.txt |` appended to the Rule conformance table of `runward/architecture.md`, immediately above `## 5. What stays open`. Builder kept at scripts/build-sig-mission.mjs. Runner: `node scripts/mutation-probe.mjs --function unsafeSignature --mission <dir> --ledger reports/mutation/probe-mission.jsonl`.

MISSION B — 'teeth', 2 signed rules, adversarial fixtures: the content does NOT match and is long enough that a regex the screen should have refused backtracks. t01 `([)a]+)+$` → `)a` repeated 30 times then `!` (61 characters); t02 `(a{2,})+$` → 60 `a` then `!`. SEARCH AIDS (design only, never a verdict — ADR-0046 decision 3). The shapes above were not guessed: scripts/sig-exhaustive.mjs, sig-structured.mjs and sig-structured2.mjs apply each mutant to dist/lib/evidence.js and diff `unsafeSignature`'s answer against the pristine one over, respectively, an exhaustive alphabet sweep (up to 48 427 560 strings per mutant), 1 414 878 regex-shaped strings, and 623 980 candidates filtered to VALID ECMAScript regexes. The last filter is what separates a mutant that only swaps one refusal message for another from a mutant that moves the gate between refusing and compiling. Every shape they proposed was then put into a real mission and judged by `runward check --strict --json`.

The mutated NESTED scan matches only when the body quantifier sits immediately before the ), so it still catches (a+)+, (a*b*)* and every reduced (G+)+ — but it stops catching a group whose quantifier is followed by more body text. Differential run over 56 054 inputs (the 9 shipped signatures, every fixture in evidence-signature.test.js, nesting depths 1-100, all strings of length <= 4 over a 16-character regex alphabet, 60 000 random ones): exactly two inputs separate mutant from original, (a+b?)+ and (a+b)+, both valid regexes, original true / mutant false. (a+b?)+ is genuinely exponential (b? is optional, so the group degenerates to (a+)+): measured, /(a+b?)+$/ against N a then ! costs 22 ms at N=20 and 87 ms at N=22, doubling per character, while /(a+b)+$/ stays at 0.05 ms. Nothing downstream catches it — the adjacent-atom scan sees two distinct atoms, and the reduction collapses the single group to G++ before the flat scan looks again. Self-gate: exit 0, 4449 bytes, byte-identical. Teeth mission (baseline exit 1, 222–229 ms): byte-identical payload, no slowdown. The same harness on the same missions DOES see this function move — it caught 13 of the 22 mutants, three of them as a gate that renders no verdict — so the null reading is a measurement, not a blind instrument. Corroborated by an exhaustive differential sweep of unsafeSignature under this mutant against the pristine one (scripts/sig-exhaustive2.mjs): 47 079 207 strings over `()a+*?|`, every length up to 9 — zero disagreement.
verdicts.argument: The mutation substitutes the literal `Stryker was here!` for an empty string inside the collapse replacement, so the string the loop builds does change. What cannot change is any predicate applied to it. That literal contains no `(`, no `)`, and none of `+`, `*`, `{`, `}`, `|`. Everything downstream is one of three readers: `NESTED` and `ALT`, whose only obligations outside `[^()]*` are `[+*}]`, `\|`, `[+*{]`, `\(` and `\)`; the collapse pattern itself, whose body class is `[^()]*`; and `/[+*}]/.test(body)`. Characters that belong to `[^()]` and to none of those sets are absorbed by an unanchored, backtracking `[^()]*` — they can neither satisfy an obligation that was unsatisfied nor break a match that held, since `*` may always give the characters back. And because the literal introduces no parenthesis, it adds no group: the loop peels the same number of levels and meets the `i < 20` budget at the same depth. The inserted text is therefore inert for every scan the function performs, on every input.

verdicts.argument: `if (next === t) break` is the loop's fixpoint test, and the mutation only removes the early exit; the loop stays bounded by `i < 20`, so it cannot run forever. Take the iteration where the guard holds. `next === t`, so `t = next` is a no-op and the following `if (flat(t)) return true` is evaluated on a value that has already been judged: on the previous iteration for any iteration after the first, and on `norm` itself — by `if (flat(norm) || flat(source)) return true`, before the loop — for the first. In both cases the judgment was `false`, because a `true` would already have returned. Every iteration the mutant adds therefore re-evaluates a decided predicate on an unchanged string, and the loop still falls out of the bottom to `return false`. The only thing that changes is work done: the same exhaustive sweep took 188 584 ms against 57 220 / 57 631 ms for its two neighbours on line 217, and both probe missions returned a byte-identical payload.

verdicts.evidence: The loop never exits by exhausting its counter, so removing one iteration removes nothing. Every pass that changes t deletes at least one ( (the replacement G[+][q] contains no parenthesis), and t starts with opens of them, so at most opens changing passes exist; the (opens+1)-th iteration can only observe next === t and break. The exit is always break or return true inside the body. verdicts.evidence: The prefix alternation is a parsing convenience, not a decision: whatever it does not consume is consumed by ([^()]*) in the same span, so the match always covers the same characters and the only observable is /[+*}]/.test(body) — whether the collapsed token keeps a +. Group-prefix characters are ? : = ! < > plus name characters, none of which is +, * or }, so folding them into body cannot flip that mark. SENSITIVITY CONTROL, exhibited rather than asserted: the mutant DOES differ where the prefix span carries the only quantifier character — a targeted sweep of 3 276 shapes found 48 such inputs, e.g. ((?+))+ (original true, mutant false). Every one of them is a SyntaxError, not a regex. And through the only production call site the verdict is identical for those — unsafeSignature false is followed immediately by new RegExp(sig, "i") in a try/catch that pushes invalid signature regex in the rule file for the same row and continues, so the row is refused, the violation count and the exit code are unchanged, and only the message wording moves. Zero valid-regex differences.
